answer: Each identity posts a 50-credit bond in the juniper registry and buys a policy from an insurer before claiming work. At every tide, insurers check a key-signed thread of work. A first policy costs 40 in premium; each further policy for the same operator costs 40 plus 15 per earlier policy. The kth fake pays 40+15(k-1) in premium, and 1,000 fakes pay 7,532,500, so total cost grows quadratically and policies are non-transferable. A captive insurer ring fails: one fake voids its policies and slashes its 20,000 stake. An honest agent pays one 40 premium and recovers its bond.
